note: Real-world application profiles. Where scenarios/ tests one atomic behavior, a profile is a COMPLETE app: its content schema, realistic seed volumes, and a weighted traffic mix that mirrors real usage. GENERATED by lyeve-examples/perf/export-profiles.mjs and committed here; do not hand-edit. Each profile mirrors the runnable example named in pairedExample, and its content types are read from a running engine rather than written twice, because writing them twice is how the previous version drifted into driving a query syntax the engine does not have. Path templates say what they sample: {id:type} and {slug:type} draw from that content type, {term} is a search word. Queries use the syntax the engine really has: filters[column]=value for exact equality, filters[<relation>_id] for a relation, no sort parameter (rows arrive created_at DESC), limit clamped to 25..200, and search on the admin router. Field types: string|text|integer|decimal|boolean|json|timestamp|media|relation(->to). presets are schema plugin presets the seeder applies before it creates the types. seedValues fixes a field for every seeded row of a type: a literal, null to leave it unset, or {id:type} for a seeded row of that type. A traffic entry with needs names the plugin it depends on, and paid says whether that plugin needs a license: a free run drives every entry that is not paid, and a licensed run (FULL=1) drives them all.

profiles.realWorld: Topics are content, and so are the replies under them, in the comments type the schema plugin's preset creates. A topic page costs one topic read plus one filtered read of its thread. This profile drives both.

profiles.name: Documentation Portal
profiles.tagline: A docs site: a deep page tree, assembled by the application.
profiles.realWorld: Nested documentation pages under a few spaces, navigated by tree and by search. The engine has no tree query, so every page load reads a flat list and the hierarchy is built in the app: this profile measures that read.

traffic.desc: read one page

profiles.name: Events and Registration
profiles.tagline: An events site: reads against a counter the application maintains.
profiles.realWorld: Remaining places are capacity minus a registered count the application keeps, because the engine has no inventory concept. Reads dominate, and each one reads a number a write path is contending for.

profiles.realWorld: Reporters draft, editors publish, and the public reads only what is published. Most of the store is not publicly visible, which is the point: the public reads are filtered and the desk reads are not.

profiles.name: GraphQL Storefront
profiles.tagline: The same catalog over GraphQL, where a page is one request.
profiles.realWorld: A storefront served entirely through GraphQL. The transport's one real advantage over the REST content API is that several root fields travel in one document, so a page that needs three collections of records costs one request instead of three. This profile measures that against the equivalent single-field read. It cannot traverse a relation, because the GraphQL surface exposes the orphan relation column and not the foreign key, so the types carry a denormalized slug instead.

postBody.query: { gql_products(limit: 25) { id title slug price_cents stock } }

traffic.desc: one root field, the GraphQL equivalent of a REST list

postBody.query: { products: gql_products(limit: 25) { id title slug price_cents } collections: gql_collections(limit: 20) { id title slug } reviews: gql_reviews(limit: 25) { id title rating } }

traffic.desc: three root fields in one document, which is the only thing this transport does that REST cannot

postBody.query: { gql_products(limit: 50) { id title slug description price_cents stock collection_slug } }

traffic.desc: a wide selection over 50 records, well inside the measured cost ceiling of 1000

profiles.name: Photo Library
profiles.tagline: A photo archive: deep albums, read constantly, written in bursts.
profiles.realWorld: A photographer's archive: a few dozen albums holding a few thousand frames, browsed far more often than added to, where every page load is a list filtered to one album followed by a read of one frame.

traffic.desc: one photograph, which is what a photo page loads before it asks for the bytes
a whole album, filtered on the foreign key because the engine cannot filter by the album's slug
a photograph with its album inflated, which is the page load in one request instead of two

profiles.realWorld: An operations knowledge base fronted by a search box: readers arrive with a query rather than a URL, type into an autocomplete on the way, and open one or two articles. Reads of a single record are the minority.

the slug lookup a result link turns into, because there is no get-by-slug route
browsing a category, filtered on the foreign key because search cannot filter a relation

profiles.name: Appointment Booking

profiles.realWorld: Patients pick a practitioner, scan the open times and book one. The engine has no availability query, so the front page and each practitioner page read up to 200 slots and decide what is open in the app.

the slot's practitioner on the booking form and on the confirmation page, the second hop populate does not take
the confirmation page: an appointment by slug with its slot inflated

profiles.name: Support Helpdesk
profiles.tagline: A support desk whose inbox reads every ticket and every reply on each view.
profiles.realWorld: Agents work a queue of tickets and the threads under them. The engine has no count and no negated filter, so the inbox pages through every ticket by status and every reply to show a reply count, and the cost of one inbox view grows with the whole desk.

traffic.desc: the first page of the inbox's status query
a later page of the same query, which the inbox reads until a page comes back short
the first page of the unfiltered reply read behind each row's reply count
a middle page of that read, which walks every reply on the desk at each inbox view
a ticket page resolves its slug, and so does each reply or status action before it writes
the thread under a ticket, filtered on the foreign key

profiles.name: Subscription Publication
profiles.tagline: A paywalled publication: each signed-in page view also reads the reader.
profiles.realWorld: Free and paid articles behind a server-side paywall. A signed-in reader's page costs one read of their member record on top of the article, because access is decided from the tier and status the payment provider last reported.

traffic.desc: an article page resolves its slug, since there is no get-by-slug route

the front page, newest first
the account page's license panel, an engine route that no plugin serves

profiles.name: Operations Dashboard
profiles.tagline: An operations console that reads the engine's own telemetry, not content.
profiles.realWorld: An operator console over the engine's request analytics, content activity, health probes, pool and latency figures, and usage and quotas. Each page fans out into five to eight telemetry reads at once, and the figures come from the traffic the engine has served, so the seed and the run fill them.
